newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: FOCUS-Slovak Nafta plan fails to please.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Slovak Nafta plan fails to please.

text.p: Slovak oil and gas storage firm Nafta a.s. announced an ambitious eight-year investment plan to shareholders on Wednesday, but analysts said the move did little to shore up the firm's sagging image.

Nafta has been surrounded by controversy since the government sold its 45.9 percent stake to privately-owned Druha Obchodna for 500 million crowns ($15.85 million), far below its market value of about 3.2 billion crowns.
Analysts had seen Wednesday's extraordinary shareholders' meeting as a chance for the company to show its vision of the firm's future, but came away less than impressed.
They said that despite unveiling a one billion crown investment programme for the next eight years, the company's owners failed to give many details of their development plan.

"They had a chance to clear up the uncertainty surrounding them, they could have shown the market their real commitment to the development of the company," one international broker who attended the meeting said. "But it seems that they have failed in this task."
The state privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (NPF), raised eyebrows in August when it sold its entire holdings in Nafta, to little-known Druha Obchodna.
The sell-off implied an average price of about 400 crowns a share, while at the time of the sale, Nafta shares stood at around 2,000 crowns on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE).
Dusan Sykora, a broker at ING Barings, said Nafta's owners had not only failed to dispell negative rumours about them, but their presentation may have further damaged Nafta's image.
"We can expect that investors will sell their holdings in Nafta, as nothing is much clearer, if not even worse," he said.

Analaysts said investor interest in Nafta shares had waned, resulting in a sharp fall in its share price. Nafta closed at 1,373 crowns on Tuesday, far below the 2,000 crown level they held at the time of the sell-off.
The investment programme announced on Wednesday includes:
*A doubling of the present gas storage capacity from two to four billion cubic metres.
*Increasing natural gas production from its own Slovak resources.
*Launching crude oil production in Kazakhstan under a joint-venture with the Kazakh company, Anacon.
